name: Kedemah
overview: Kedemah is a male figure identified as the twelfth-born son of Ishmael, belonging to the tribe of Kedemah. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or details about his life or actions. His identity is primarily established through his lineage within the family of Ishmael.
namesAndTitles: The name Kedemah means "east" in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given to him. This meaning is straightforward and does not imply any special title or divine naming but simply identifies him as recorded in Genesis 25:15.
familyAndRelationships: Kedemah is explicitly recorded as a son of Ishmael, making him part of the Ishmaelite lineage. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further details about his family connections or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Kedemah's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Ishmael, which is important for understanding the broader narrative of God's covenantal promises and the fulfillment of His plans through Abraham's descendants. While he does not have a prominent role or recorded deeds, his inclusion in the biblical record underscores the faithfulness of Scripture in preserving the genealogies that trace God's providential work.
